technical_and_design_decisions: Implement deployment properties as optional key-value configuration while preserving existing behavior when properties are absent.
Interpret {{count}} as an instance-count expansion for modules whose generated instances share the same environment variables; keep the deployment property model backward compatible.
Use the existing repository build, test, documentation, and CI conventions rather than introducing new build or deployment infrastructure.
Fix the Kafka binder at the existing Spring Cloud Stream integration boundary and validate it against an operational Kafka broker using automated integration tests.
Implement RxJava processor support as a Spring Cloud Stream-compatible module using the project's existing module and messaging conventions.
Create the shell startup banner as a static Spring Cloud Data Flow banner resource and integrate it through the existing shell startup mechanism.

Publish documentation through the existing GitHub Pages workflow and document the architecture, deployment-version differences, Concourse CI findings, and Cloud Foundry deployment guidance in repository documentation.
assumptions: The existing s-c-d and s-c-s-m repositories, build environments, CI jobs, and documentation tooling are available and can be modified without repository migration.

The specification refers to Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d), Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s), and Spring Cloud Stream modules (s-c-s-m); exact repository names and branch policies follow the existing project conventions.
No major framework upgrade, Java version migration, or redesign of the deployment model is required for this increment.
For the Kafka binder work, a compatible Kafka broker and test environment are available; provisioning or operating production Kafka infrastructure is outside scope.
The Kafka issue is a localized binder defect rather than a complete binder rewrite, and existing binder tests can be extended.
RxJava processor support uses an already available RxJava dependency or a standard compatible version; development of a new reactive programming abstraction is outside scope.
Documentation is reviewed by the developer and validated with local builds or link checks where available; formal technical-writing or product-management review is outside scope.
The Concourse CI story requires a focused technical investigation and documented recommendations or a small proof of concept, not production CI migration.
Effort includes implementation, automated tests, local validation, documentation updates, and normal code-review preparation, but excludes waiting time for external approvals.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the relevant s-c-d, s-c-s, and module repositories; trace deployment-property handling, Kafka binder integration, shell startup, documentation publishing, and existing test conventions; define acceptance checks and implementation boundaries.

Add optional deployment key-value properties, implement {{count}} expansion for multiple module instances sharing environment variables, preserve existing deployment behavior, and add unit and integration coverage for single-instance, multi-instance, missing-property, and invalid-input cases.

Create and configure the gh_pages branches for the s-c-d and s-c-s-m repositories, align branch protection or publishing configuration with existing project practices, and verify that documentation can be pushed through pull requests.

Reproduce the Kafka binder failure, inspect configuration and message-binding lifecycle behavior, implement the smallest compatible fix, and add or update automated tests including an operational-broker integration validation.
Document the s-c-d architecture, identify the relevant deployment components, and describe the deployment differences between 1.x and 2.x with diagrams or structured reference material where useful.

Study Concourse CI concepts and pipeline configuration, assess how it could support s-c-d development and release workflows, run a limited proof of concept or configuration exercise, and record findings and recommendations.

Implement or adapt an RxJava processor module for Spring Cloud Stream, connect it to the established input/output binding conventions, add functional and configuration tests, and provide basic usage documentation.

Create the new Spring Cloud Data Flow banner asset, integrate it with shell-server startup using the existing resource and configuration mechanism, and verify rendering in supported console startup paths.

Write and integrate the README documentation for running on Cloud Foundry, including prerequisites, deployment steps, configuration, operational considerations, and links to relevant commands or resources.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature validation and documentation publishing checks
activities.activity_description: Run repository builds, unit tests, integration tests, documentation generation, link or formatting checks, and representative end-to-end validation across deployment properties, Kafka binding, RxJava processing, banner startup, and GitHub Pages publishing.

activities.activity_name: Code cleanup, review preparation, and delivery
activities.activity_description: Refine implementation and documentation, update changelog or release notes where required, prepare commits and pull requests, address local review findings, and confirm that all story acceptance evidence is included.
